role.en: ruler of an empire "on which the sun never sets"

bio.en: Grandson of Maximilian I and Ferdinand of Aragon, he ruled Spain and its American colonies, the Netherlands and the empire. He outlawed Luther at the Diet of Worms in 1521, was the last emperor crowned by a pope (1530), and in 1556 abdicated and retired to the monastery of Yuste.
Won the Inca civil war against his brother Huáscar, then was captured by Pizarro at Cajamarca and executed despite a vast ransom.

role.en: emperor of the Peace of Augsburg who held Vienna against Suleiman

bio.en: Younger brother of Charles V, king of Bohemia and Hungary from 1526. Vienna withstood Suleiman the Magnificent's siege under him in 1529, and in 1555 he concluded the religious Peace of Augsburg on the principle "whose realm, his religion".
A Ruthenian captive who became the legal wife of Suleiman the Magnificent, unprecedented in Ottoman history; a powerful courtier and patron.
General of the Adal Sultanate who conquered most of Ethiopia before falling in battle against an Ethiopian–Portuguese army.
Leading Reformation theologian whose Calvinism turned Geneva into a 'Protestant Rome' and spread to Scotland, the Netherlands and beyond.

role.en: shogun forever fleeing his own capital

bio.en: He became shogun in 1521 at the age of ten. Caught up in the feuds of the Hosokawa and Miyoshi, he repeatedly fled Kyoto for Ōmi under Rokkaku protection; in 1546 he passed the office to his son and died in exile.

role.en: 'Bloody Mary', who returned England to Catholicism

bio.en: Daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon, the first queen to rule England in her own right. She restored Catholicism and burned some 280 Protestants at the stake; she married Philip II of Spain and lost Calais.
Spent nearly 30 years compiling the Bencao Gangmu, a vast materia medica describing almost 1,900 medicinal substances.
Florentine wife of Henry II and mother of three French kings, the power behind the throne during the Wars of Religion and St Bartholomew's Day massacre.

role.en: king mortally wounded in a jousting tournament

bio.en: Husband of Catherine de’ Medici. He took Calais from the English (1558) and ended the Italian Wars with the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis, but was fatally wounded by a lance to the eye at a tournament celebrating it.

role.en: sultan who took Cyprus and lost at Lepanto

bio.en: Son of Suleiman and Hurrem and the first sultan not to lead his armies in person, he ruled through Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha. Cyprus was conquered and the fleet destroyed at Lepanto in 1571.
Founded a major observatory in Istanbul (demolished in 1580), built precise astronomical clocks and described an early steam turbine.
Ruled an empire 'on which the sun never set', including Portugal and the Philippines. Built El Escorial and sent the Armada against England.

role.en: tolerant emperor who sympathised with the Protestants

bio.en: Son of Ferdinand I, so sympathetic to the Lutherans that his father feared he would convert. As emperor he kept the religious peace, allowed Protestant worship to the Austrian nobility, and in 1575 was elected by one faction to the Polish throne.
First ruler crowned Tsar of All Russia. Conquered Kazan and Astrakhan, unleashed the Oprichnina terror and waged the long Livonian War.
Poet-saint who retold the Ramayana in vernacular Awadhi; his Ramcharitmanas remains one of India's most widely read books.
Cossack ataman hired by the Stroganovs who defeated Khan Kuchum's Siberian Khanate, beginning Russia's conquest of Siberia.

role.en: King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania

bio.en: Prince of Transylvania elected to the throne of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1576. Turned the Livonian War against Muscovy, besieged Pskov and founded the Vilnius Academy.
Last of the Tudors. Her reign saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada and a golden age of English drama and seafaring.
First of Japan's three great unifiers, who pioneered mass use of firearms and conquered central Japan before dying in a betrayal.

Shogun from 1546 and a pupil of the swordmaster Tsukahara Bokuden. He tried to restore the shogunate's prestige, mediating among daimyo and receiving the Portuguese, but in 1565 he was killed in his residence by the Miyoshi trio and Matsunaga Hisahide.
Peasant's son who rose to rule all Japan, completing its unification, building Osaka Castle and twice invading Korea.

role.en: boy king who established Protestantism in England

bio.en: Henry VIII's only legitimate son, crowned at nine. Under him England turned Protestant, adopting the English Book of Common Prayer. He died at 15 after trying to leave the throne to Lady Jane Grey.

role.en: last Ashikaga shogun, expelled by Nobunaga

bio.en: Yoshiteru's brother, put in power by Oda Nobunaga in 1568. Chafing at being a puppet, he organised daimyo coalitions against his patron and was expelled from Kyoto in 1573, the date usually taken as the end of the Muromachi shogunate.
Yoshiteru's cousin, appointed shogun in 1568 at the Miyoshi clan's behest. He never reached the capital and died of illness months later, as Oda Nobunaga entered Kyoto with his rival Yoshiaki.

role.en: chronicler, son of a conquistador and an Inca princess

bio.en: The first great writer born in Latin America; his Royal Commentaries on Inca history were published in Spain, and he died the same year as Cervantes and Shakespeare.
Queen of Scots from six days old. Fled to England after a rebellion, was held captive for 19 years and executed on Elizabeth I's orders.
Unified most of India, built an efficient administration, pursued religious tolerance and was a great patron of the arts.
Won the Battle of Sekigahara (1600) and founded the Tokugawa shogunate, giving Japan 250 years of peace with Edo (Tokyo) as its seat.

role.en: teenage husband of Mary, Queen of Scots, who reigned 17 months

bio.en: He became king at 15, but power lay with the Guise brothers, uncles of his wife Mary Stuart. The Huguenot Conspiracy of Amboise was crushed in his reign; he died at 16 of an ear infection.
Admiral who crushed the Japanese navy during the Imjin War using 'turtle ships' and fell in the war's final battle.

role.en: sultan who won the Caucasus from the Safavids

bio.en: He ruled without leaving the palace; the Safavid war of 1578–1590 brought Georgia, Shirvan and Tabriz. He granted trade privileges to England and began the Long War with the Habsburgs.
Author of Don Quixote, one of the first and greatest modern novels. Fought at Lepanto and spent five years as a captive in Algiers.
Saadi sultan who beat the Portuguese at the Battle of the Three Kings, conquered the Songhai Empire and corresponded with Elizabeth I.

role.en: king of the St Bartholomew’s Day massacre

bio.en: He became king at ten under the regency of his mother, Catherine de’ Medici. He sanctioned the St Bartholomew’s Day massacre of Huguenots in 1572 and died of tuberculosis aged 23.

role.en: last Valois king, stabbed by a monk

bio.en: Before taking the French throne he was briefly king of Poland (1573–1574). Amid the Wars of Religion he had the Duke of Guise murdered and was himself stabbed by the friar Jacques Clément, naming Henry of Navarre his heir.
De facto regent under Tsar Feodor, then elected tsar himself. Established the Moscow Patriarchate; his death opened the Time of Troubles.
Jesuit who was the first European admitted to the Forbidden City, bringing Western science and maps to China and China to Europe.

role.en: patron emperor who gathered Kepler, Brahe and Arcimboldo in Prague

bio.en: He moved his court to Prague and made it a capital of art, science and alchemy, employing Tycho Brahe, Johannes Kepler and Giuseppe Arcimboldo and amassing a famous Kunstkammer. Reclusive and melancholic, he gradually lost power to his brother Matthias.

role.en: boyar tsar of the Time of Troubles who died in Polish captivity

bio.en: A boyar who led the plot against False Dmitry I and was chosen tsar. He fought Bolotnikov's rebellion and False Dmitry II; deposed in 1610, he was forcibly tonsured and handed to the Poles, dying in their captivity.

role.en: first Bourbon king, who issued the Edict of Nantes

bio.en: A Huguenot leader who converted to Catholicism to win the throne ("Paris is well worth a Mass"). His Edict of Nantes of 1598 ended the Wars of Religion; he was assassinated by the fanatic Ravaillac.
A jurist and author of over 40 books with a huge library; taken to Marrakesh after the Moroccan conquest, he later returned to Timbuktu.

role.en: emperor under whom the Defenestration of Prague began the Thirty Years' War

bio.en: Brother of Rudolf II, who wrested Austria, Hungary and then Bohemia from him in the "Brothers' Quarrel". He moved the court back to Vienna; in 1618 Bohemian Protestants threw his regents out of a window in Prague Castle, starting the Thirty Years' War.

role.en: last Rurikid tsar, under whom the Moscow Patriarchate was founded

bio.en: Son of Ivan the Terrible, frail and pious; the country was effectively run by his brother-in-law Boris Godunov. The Moscow Patriarchate was created in 1589, and the Rurik dynasty died out with Feodor.
United the Jurchen tribes, created the Eight Banners and founded the Later Jin state that became the Qing Empire.

Father of empiricism: knowledge should be built from experience and observation, reasoning from facts to conclusions (induction), not from authority. "Knowledge is power" is attributed to him. Lord Chancellor of England.
The greatest playwright in the English language, author of Hamlet, Romeo and Juliet, King Lear and Macbeth, staged at London's Globe Theatre.
First to turn a telescope to the sky, discovering Jupiter's moons and the phases of Venus. Defended Copernicus and was condemned by the Inquisition.

role.en: Scottish king who united the crowns of England and Scotland

bio.en: Son of Mary, Queen of Scots, and king of Scotland from the age of one, he inherited the English throne in 1603 as the first Stuart. He survived the Gunpowder Plot of 1605; his reign gave us the King James Bible and the founding of Jamestown.

role.en: sultan who executed 19 brothers and won at Keresztes

bio.en: On his accession in 1595 he had his 19 brothers put to death. He led the campaign in Hungary in person and defeated the imperial army at Keresztes in 1596.
'Father of New France' who founded Quebec in 1608 and explored the St Lawrence valley and the Great Lakes.
Discovered the three laws of planetary motion on elliptical orbits using Tycho Brahe's observations while imperial mathematician in Prague.
Greatest Safavid shah: reformed the army, won back lands from Ottomans and Portuguese and made Isfahan one of the world's finest capitals.
Favourite wife of Emperor Jahangir who effectively ran the empire, with coins struck in her name; a patron of architecture and gardens.
With Kuzma Minin led the Second Volunteer Army that freed Moscow from Polish occupation in 1612, ending the Time of Troubles.

role.en: zealous Catholic who crushed the Bohemian revolt in the Thirty Years' War

bio.en: Jesuit-educated champion of the Counter-Reformation. After the victory at the White Mountain in 1620 he executed the Bohemian rebel leaders and forcibly re-Catholicised Bohemia; he relied on Wallenstein's army, and his Edict of Restitution of 1629 only prolonged the war.

role.en: second Tokugawa shogun, who locked in the house's grip on the daimyo

bio.en: Shogun 1605–1623 and Ieyasu's son. With his father he took Osaka (1615), issued the Laws for the Military Houses that bound the daimyo, and harshly persecuted Christians, culminating in the Great Genna Martyrdom of 1622.

role.en: pretender who claimed to be Tsarevich Dmitry

bio.en: A pretender usually identified with the runaway monk Grigory Otrepyev. With Polish backing he took the throne in 1605, married Marina Mniszech and was killed by rebellious Muscovites a year later.
Mbundu queen who resisted Portuguese colonisation and the slave trade for decades as a skilled diplomat and war leader.
In Leviathan he described the state of nature as a "war of all against all", which people escape by handing power to a strong state through a social contract.
Wife of Ahmed I and mother of two sultans who for decades effectively governed the Ottoman Empire during the 'Sultanate of Women'.

role.en: sultan who built the Blue Mosque

bio.en: He came to the throne at 13 and broke with the custom of fratricide, sparing his brother Mustafa. He made the Peace of Zsitvatorok with the Habsburgs (1606) and built the Sultan Ahmed (Blue) Mosque in Istanbul.
His reign was the golden age of Mughal architecture: he built the Taj Mahal for his wife and Delhi's Red Fort. Deposed by his son Aurangzeb.
Follower of Caravaggio and first woman admitted to Florence's Academy of Drawing, famed for dramatic works like Judith Slaying Holofernes.
Beloved wife of Shah Jahan who died giving birth to their 14th child; the Taj Mahal was built as her tomb.
Made Sweden a great power and revolutionised warfare. Led the Protestant cause in the Thirty Years' War and fell at the Battle of Lützen.
Led the 1648 Cossack uprising against the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, founded the Hetmanate and accepted the Tsar's protection at Pereiaslav in 1654.
Father of modern philosophy ('I think, therefore I am') and inventor of analytic geometry; spent most of his career in the Dutch Republic.
Powhatan chief's daughter linked to the early Jamestown colony; she married settler John Rolfe and died in England.

role.en: first tsar of the Romanov dynasty

bio.en: Elected by the Zemsky Sobor in 1613, ending the Time of Troubles. He concluded the Treaty of Stolbovo with Sweden (1617) and the Truce of Deulino with Poland (1618); for years his father, Patriarch Filaret, co-ruled the country.
Parliamentary leader in the English Civil War whose New Model Army defeated the royalists; ruled as Lord Protector after Charles I's execution.
Ethiopian thinker whose treatise Hatata ("Inquiry") urged testing every religious teaching by reason and asserted the equality of all people, women included. Some scholars dispute his authorship.

role.en: king executed by Parliament after the Civil War

bio.en: His attempt to rule without Parliament led to the Civil War of 1642–1651. Defeated by Cromwell's New Model Army, he was tried for treason and beheaded in London on 30 January 1649.

The brother of Ahmed I, he spent years confined in the palace 'cage'. Enthroned in 1617 and deposed after three months, he became sultan again in 1622 after the murder of Osman II, only to be deposed once more.

role.en: king who ruled alongside Cardinal Richelieu

bio.en: Son of Henry IV. From 1624 he relied on Cardinal Richelieu, who took the Huguenot stronghold of La Rochelle and brought France into the Thirty Years’ War against the Habsburgs.
Expelled the Jesuits, restored Orthodoxy in Ethiopia and founded the new capital of Gondar with its castle, Fasil Ghebbi.
First European to reach Tasmania, New Zealand, Tonga and Fiji; Tasmania and the Tasman Sea are named after him.

role.en: shogun who closed Japan to the Europeans

bio.en: Shogun 1623–1651. He made daimyo spend alternate years in Edo (sankin-kōtai), crushed the Christian Shimabara Rebellion (1637–1638), expelled the Portuguese and left only the Dutch, on Dejima, to trade with Europe.

role.en: young sultan murdered by the Janissaries

bio.en: After the failed siege of Khotyn in 1621 he planned to replace the Janissaries with a new army; they rose in revolt and strangled him in Yedikule, the first regicide in the dynasty's history.
Supreme master of the Dutch Golden Age and of light and shadow: The Night Watch, The Return of the Prodigal Son and dozens of self-portraits.

role.en: emperor who signed the Peace of Westphalia

bio.en: Son of Ferdinand II, nominal commander of the imperial victory at Nördlingen in 1634. Inheriting a war-ravaged empire, he accepted the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, which entrenched the independence of the German princes; he also composed music.
Spent forty years travelling the Ottoman Empire and beyond, recording it all in his ten-volume Book of Travels.

role.en: sultan who retook Baghdad and banned tobacco

bio.en: Enthroned as a child under the regency of his mother Kösem, he later restored order ruthlessly and banned tobacco, coffee and wine. In 1638 he retook Baghdad from the Safavids; the Treaty of Zuhab (1639) fixed the border with Iran for centuries.

The only surviving brother of Murad IV, he spent his youth in fear of execution and became known for extravagance and caprice. The war with Venice for Crete began under him; in 1648 he was deposed and strangled.
Under him the Mughal Empire reached its greatest extent. A devout Muslim, he fought draining wars against the Marathas.
Ming loyalist who fought the Manchus and in 1662 expelled the Dutch from Taiwan, founding his own kingdom there.

role.en: tsar of the 1649 Law Code and the church schism

bio.en: The second Romanov tsar. His reign saw the 1649 Law Code that bound peasants to the land, the union with Left-bank Ukraine (1654), and Patriarch Nikon's reforms that led to the church schism.
Maratha leader and master of guerrilla war against the Mughals, crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 as founder of the Maratha state.

Son of the executed Charles I, he returned to the throne in 1660 in the Restoration of the monarchy. Known as the Merry Monarch, he saw London through the Great Plague of 1665 and the Great Fire of 1666 and chartered the Royal Society.

Taught that God and Nature are one and the same single substance, and that freedom lies in understanding necessity. Expelled from Amsterdam's Jewish community, he ground lenses for a living; his Ethics appeared after his death.

Held that the mind starts as a "blank slate" and all knowledge comes from experience, and that government is legitimate only with the consent of the governed, who keep rights to life, liberty and property. Shaped the US Declaration of Independence.

role.en: last Catholic king, deposed in the Glorious Revolution

bio.en: Brother of Charles II; as Duke of York he gave his name to New York. His efforts to restore Catholic rights provoked the Glorious Revolution of 1688, which put his daughter Mary and her husband William of Orange on the throne; James died in exile in France.

role.en: King of France, the Sun King

bio.en: Reigned 72 years, longer than any other European monarch. Embodied absolutism, built Versailles and made France the dominant power.

role.en: emperor under whom Vienna was saved from the Turks and Hungary retaken

bio.en: In 1683 Vienna, besieged by Kara Mustafa's army, was relieved by Jan Sobieski. The ensuing Great Turkish War ended with the Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699, which gave the Habsburgs almost all of Hungary; late in life he began the War of the Spanish Succession.

role.en: shogun under whom samurai rule turned civilian

bio.en: He became shogun in 1651 at the age of ten, with regents led by Hoshina Masayuki governing. He lived through the Great Fire of Meireki (1657), which destroyed most of Edo, and in 1663 banned retainers from following their lord in death.

role.en: sultan of the Köprülü era and the siege of Vienna

bio.en: Sultan at six, he left the state to the Köprülü grand viziers, who took Candia (1669) and Podolia (1672). After the rout at Vienna in 1683 and defeats in Hungary he was deposed in 1687.

role.en: sultan who retook Belgrade after 39 years in the 'cage'

bio.en: He spent 39 years confined in the palace before taking the throne amid the war with the Holy League. His grand vizier Fazıl Mustafa Pasha Köprülü recaptured Belgrade in 1690.
Formulated universal gravitation and the laws of motion, co-invented calculus and explained the colour spectrum, founding classical physics.

role.en: sultan who lost the Battle of Slankamen

bio.en: He reigned four years during the war with the Holy League; in 1691 his army was routed at Slankamen and Grand Vizier Fazıl Mustafa Pasha was killed. The Ottomans lost most of Hungary.
The supreme master of haiku, who raised the form to high art; author of the travel journal The Narrow Road to the Deep North.
Alaouite sultan who reigned 55 years, built an army of Black slave soldiers, took Tangier from the English and rebuilt Meknes as his capital.
Invented calculus independently of Newton and developed binary arithmetic. Advised Peter the Great on founding an Academy of Sciences.

role.en: the 'Dog Shogun' who outlawed cruelty to animals

bio.en: Shogun 1680–1709, a zealous Confucian and Buddhist. His Laws of Compassion for Living Things punished cruelty to dogs; his era saw the flowering of Genroku urban culture and the affair of the 47 rōnin (1701–1703).

name.en: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz

bio.en: Nun, poet and scholar of New Spain, called the 'Tenth Muse', who defended women's right to learning.

role.en: Dutch stadtholder who took power in the Glorious Revolution

bio.en: Stadtholder of the Dutch Republic who landed in England in 1688 and ruled jointly with his wife Mary II. He accepted the Bill of Rights of 1689, limiting royal power, and defeated James II at the Battle of the Boyne in Ireland.
China's longest-reigning emperor (61 years). Consolidated Qing rule, annexed Taiwan and signed the Treaty of Nerchinsk with Russia.
United the Akan states and founded the Ashanti Empire with its capital at Kumasi; by legend the Golden Stool became the symbol of the nation.

role.en: Elector of Hanover, first king of the Hanoverian dynasty

bio.en: A German elector who inherited the British throne as the nearest Protestant relative. Speaking little English and taking little part in government, he let power pass to ministers led by Robert Walpole, the first prime minister.

role.en: tsar who abolished the precedence system (mestnichestvo)

bio.en: Eldest son of Alexis and elder half-brother of Peter the Great. In 1682 he abolished mestnichestvo and burned the precedence books; his reign saw the Russo-Turkish war ended by the Treaty of Bakhchisarai.

role.en: shogun who repealed Tsunayoshi's dog laws

bio.en: Tsunayoshi's nephew, shogun 1709–1712. He immediately repealed the Laws of Compassion and, with his Confucian adviser Arai Hakuseki, began restoring the debased coinage and curbing the outflow of silver and gold abroad.

role.en: sultan who signed the Treaty of Karlowitz

bio.en: He led his armies against the Habsburgs in person but was routed by Eugene of Savoy at Zenta in 1697. The Treaty of Karlowitz (1699) ceded Hungary and Transylvania, the empire's first major losses; he was deposed in the Edirne Event of 1703.

role.en: last Stuart monarch, under whom Great Britain was created

bio.en: Last monarch of the House of Stuart. Under the Acts of Union of 1707 England and Scotland merged into the Kingdom of Great Britain, and in the War of the Spanish Succession the Duke of Marlborough won at Blenheim. None of her children outlived her.
Westernised Russia through sweeping reforms, built a navy, defeated Sweden in the Great Northern War and founded Saint Petersburg.

Under him the army trapped Peter I on the Prut (1711), and after the Peace of Passarowitz (1718) came the 'Tulip Era' of palaces, gardens and İbrahim Müteferrika's first Ottoman press. He was deposed by the Patrona Halil revolt in 1730.
Venetian violinist-priest and master of the Baroque concerto, whose The Four Seasons is among the most performed works of classical music.

role.en: emperor of the War of the Spanish Succession, dead of smallpox at 32

bio.en: Eldest son of Leopold I. Allied with Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy, he fought Louis XIV successfully and put down Rákóczi's Hungarian uprising, but died suddenly of smallpox in 1711, leaving no sons.
Dane who led Russia's Kamchatka expeditions, sailed the strait between Asia and America and reached Alaska; the strait and sea bear his name.

role.en: last British king to lead troops into battle

bio.en: In 1743 he personally led his army at Dettingen, the last British monarch to do so. His reign saw the Jacobite rising of 1745 crushed and, in the Seven Years' War, Britain win Canada and strengthen its hold on India.
Led the Antonian movement calling for the reunification of the war-torn Kingdom of Kongo; burned as a heretic aged 22.

role.en: reforming shogun who allowed Western books

bio.en: Shogun 1716–1745. His Kyōhō Reforms cut spending and repaired the treasury; his care for rice prices earned him the name 'Rice Shogun'. He set up a petition box and in 1720 eased the ban on European books, opening the way for 'Dutch learning'.

role.en: first Russian empress, widow of Peter the Great

bio.en: Born Marta Skavronska, a Livonian commoner who became Peter the Great's wife. Placed on the throne by the guards and Menshikov, she created the Supreme Privy Council and saw the Academy of Sciences open.
Pinnacle of Baroque music: St Matthew Passion, The Well-Tempered Clavier, the Brandenburg Concertos. Long served as cantor in Leipzig.

role.en: emperor of the Pragmatic Sanction, who left his realms to Maria Theresa

bio.en: In the War of the Spanish Succession he claimed the Spanish throne as "Charles III". Lacking sons, he named his daughter Maria Theresa heir by the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 and spent his life seeking its recognition; he built the Karlskirche in Vienna.
Turkoman general who expelled the Afghans from Iran and seized the throne; in 1739 he sacked Delhi and carried off the Peacock Throne.

role.en: empress who tore up the Conditions; era of Biron's dominance

bio.en: Niece of Peter the Great and dowager duchess of Courland. She tore up the Supreme Privy Council's Conditions limiting her power and returned the court to St Petersburg; her favourite Biron wielded vast influence.
Leading voice of the Enlightenment who fought religious intolerance and championed free thought; author of Candide and correspondent of Catherine II.

role.en: sultan who regained Belgrade by the 1739 peace

bio.en: Brought to power by the Patrona Halil revolt, he soon crushed the rebels. With the Frenchman Bonneval (Ahmed Pasha) he modernised the artillery, and the Treaty of Belgrade (1739) won Belgrade back from Austria.

role.en: Bavarian elector, the only non-Habsburg emperor in three centuries

bio.en: Elector Charles Albert of Bavaria, who challenged Maria Theresa's inheritance. Backed by France and Prussia, he was elected emperor in 1742, but almost at once the Austrians took Munich, and he spent most of his reign in exile in Frankfurt.

role.en: sultan who spent 50 years in the 'cage'

bio.en: He took the throne at 55 after half a century of palace confinement and was known for his aversion to music and women. He completed the baroque Nuruosmaniye Mosque.
